en: The Abandoned Camp

A camp in a side chamber, left in a hurry. The fire is cold. The tent still stands, one pole leaning.

Bedrolls, a cooking pot, a bag half unpacked. Nobody came back for any of it.
Sleep in the tent

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: In the night, something walks around the tent. Then it stops walking.

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en:
You sleep. Nobody comes.

In the morning the camp is exactly as they left it.
Look around the camp

Behind the tent, half under the bedrolls, you find one of them.

His sword is out of its sheath. The blade is clean. There is not a mark on him.

He did not die fighting. His face looks as if he saw a ghost.
Take his backpack

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en:
You are still crouched over him when the tent flap moves behind you.

There is no wind down here.

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: Nothing moves. You leave him the rest.
Take his sword
Take his armor
Bury him and pray

You leave his things where they are. The ground is soft enough.

When you finish the prayer, the chamber is very quiet. You stand up lighter than you knelt down.
Leave him
You leave him as you found him. You do not look at his face again.
Leave the camp
You leave the camp as it is. Whoever left it is not coming back.

A small black music box lies under the rubble — lid cracked, one brass leg twitching.

As you lean in, it plays three notes and snaps shut.
Force it open
You pry at the lid.
Open it carefully

The lock gives. Inside, where the cylinder should turn, a cog is missing.

The box looks at you — somehow — then grows two more legs and falls in behind you.
Leave it alone

You step over it and keep walking.

Ten steps later: small metal feet on the stones behind you.
A goblin steps out from behind a broken machine, sniffs the air, and coughs.
"Snatch Box. Charge went first. I can smell the powder from here. Nothing left to seat a cog in."
He looks at your boots as if a box might still be hiding there. It is not.

A goblin steps out from behind a broken machine and points at the music box.

"Sleepy Snatch Box. Old robber model. Plays a song, puffs smoke, hero sleeps, pockets empty. Very illegal. Very profitable."

The box hides behind your boot.
"You found its heart cog. Give it here — I can seat it properly. Or improperly. Depends on payment."
"No cog? I have spares. Spare parts cost extra."
Refuse to pay
Give him an unwanted card for spare parts
Pay 30 coins for full repair

He shrugs. "Ash is ash. I don't do funerals."

He is already back behind the machine before you turn away.
The Mirror Twin

A dry corner. You sit down and shut your eyes.

When you open them, someone is sitting across from you. Hooded, cross-legged, wearing your face. The scar on your chin is on his other side.

You scratch your nose. He scratches his nose. His knees touch yours.
Give him a shard
He holds the shard up. A face looks back from it, not yours. He turns to look closer.
Sneak away

You lift your pack one strap at a time and back out of the corner. He doesn't look up.

On the sixth step the floor stops.

You land on old rugs beside a dead camp. A note under a stone: "Day 4. Mirror man STILL here. Going to try sneaking. Don't look back."

Under it, an amulet. You take it and climb out the far side. You don't look back.
Give him the Gemseeker's Lens
Even better: his own face, enormous. He presses his nose to it and forgets you.
Give him the Hand Mirror

He looks into the mirror. Another him looks back. He leans in. So does the other one.

Whoosh.

You pick up the mirror. Your reflection isn't in it. He is, pressed flat against the glass, looking pleased.
Try to out-stare him
You blink first. He does a small victory dance and wanders off, still dancing. You do not get your rest.
A shadow crosses the nest. Then again, lower.
A nest sits wedged between two fallen pillars — speckled eggs, bent keys, old buttons, and one small brass cog.
Search the nest
You reach into the nest.
The Old Chute

A flagstone tips under your boot. You drop into an old trap chute and slide a long way down in the dark.

Whatever was meant to be waiting at the bottom rotted away years ago. You land unhurt, on something that goes crack.

Under you is a spider the size of a dog, made of clear crystal. Most of it is in pieces now.
Take a crystal leg

One leg came off clean. It is cold, and it still catches the light.

Ahead of you, in the corner of the pit, is her nest: a heap of crystal eggs, each the size of a fist.
Burn the eggs

The fireball fills the pit. The eggs pop one by one.

When the smoke clears, the heat has fused what is left into a single lump of crystal.
Smash the eggs

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en:
The third egg is already open. So is the fourth.

Small crystal legs come out of the heap.

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en:
You crush them all. It is loud, and nothing answers.

The shards are worth something.
Take one egg

You pick the smallest one. It is cold, and heavier than it looks.

Something inside taps back.
Leave the nest

You leave the eggs where they are and climb out the long way.

Halfway up, below you, one of them cracks.
Leave her be

You climb off her and leave her where she lies.

Ahead of you, in the corner of the pit, is her nest: a heap of crystal eggs, each the size of a fist.
Read the scratches on the wall
Someone scratched a map into the stone, one passage circled twice. You copy it down.
The Robbed Traveller

A man sits against the wall with his pack turned out beside him. His eyes are half shut. He sees you and tries to stand, and can't.

"There was a stand," he says. "Soup. Nobody there." He laughs, and it turns into a yawn. "They took everything."
Give him your Antidote

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: He drinks it in one go. After a while his eyes open properly and he sits up straight.

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: He has nothing left to pay you with, except the one thing they missed. He unpicks his collar and puts it in your hand.

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: He unpicks his collar to pay you, and finds it empty. He looks at you for a long time. "Thank you," he says.
Cast Restoration on him

kind: outcome (one of several, chosen by the game)
en: You hold the card over him. The light goes into him and he sits up straight.
Ask what happened

"Three of them. A stand, a pot." He yawns. "Green scarves. I had one bowl and woke up like this. They took my antidotes."

He tells you where they sleep. It isn't far.
Give him food

He eats, and perks up enough to talk.

"My purse is in the lining," he says, and tells you where the gang sleeps. Then he nods off again, smiling.
Search his pack

There is a purse sewn into the lining. He watches you cut it out, too sleepy to stop you.

"Of course," he mumbles. "Of course you would."
You leave him dozing against the wall. He will wake up eventually.
The Soup Stand

A wooden stand against the wall. On it, a pot of soup, still steaming, a ladle and two clean bowls.

You call out. Nobody answers. You call again, louder. Nothing.
Eat the soup

It is good soup. You have a second bowl.

Halfway through it your fingers go numb, and you understand why nobody was minding the stand. Too late.

When you wake up the pot is gone, and so is half your purse.
Wait out of sight

You step behind the wall and wait. The soup goes on steaming.

Three men in green scarves come back for it. The cook lifts his ladle, looks at the two clean bowls, then at your wall.
Leave it and keep going
You leave the soup where it is and keep walking. Behind you it goes on steaming.
Kick the pot over

You kick the pot off the stand. Soup runs across the stones. The first rat to lick it falls asleep on the spot.

The stand tips over with it. Nailed to the underside is a purse: whatever the last few customers were carrying.

You take it and keep walking.
The Webbed Corridor

The corridor ahead is strung across with webs. The strands are thin and clear, and they catch the light like glass.

Small crystal spiders sit along them, a dozen at least, each about the size of your hand. The ones nearest you turn to watch.
Cut through the webs

The first strand you cut rings like a wire.

Every spider on the web turns toward you at once.
Go round through the rubble

There is a gap where the wall has fallen in. You squeeze through it on your stomach and come out bleeding from both elbows.

A strand of web has caught on your sleeve. By the time you pick it off, it has gone hard and clear.
Toss them some food

The food lands on the web and the nearest spiders are on it before it stops shaking.

The rest climb up out of the way. Where they were sitting, the web has left a few shards of crystal behind.
Turn back
You go back the way you came. Behind you, something ticks along the strands.
The Silk Cache

The passage widens into a low chamber. Silk hangs in sheets from the ceiling, and beneath it the floor is crowded with pale cocoons — some the size of a fist, some large enough to hold a man.

Scattered between them: a buckled breastplate, a snapped spear, a glove still shaped around an empty hand. Someone fought here. Someone lost.

The cocoons twitch when you breathe too loud.
Leave quietly

You ease back into the corridor without touching a strand.

Behind you the silk settles, and the twitching stops.
Search the cocoons

You draw a blade and step into the silk.

The nearest cocoon does not open when you cut it — it resists, tough as wet leather. You will have to break them properly.
Burn them all!

The fireball takes the chamber in one breath.

Silk blackens. Cocoons split and collapse. When the smoke thins, three scorched prizes lie open on the stone — and nothing moves to claim them.
The Lost Porter

A side corridor has gone white with old web. Halfway along it, a man hangs upside down, wrapped to the armpits, holding a frying pan.

"Oh! Hello! Have you seen my party? They told me to hold the rope while they scouted ahead. So I held it."

He lifts the end of the rope. It has been cut clean through.

"Must have snapped. Anyway, I think I'm lost."
Give him your spare armor

You cut him down and help him into the armor. It is far too big. The helmet turns when he turns his head, a little after.

"It's like wearing a house," he says happily, and knocks on his own chest.
Take the map

"I don't think I'm cut out for adventuring," he says. "Ma said so. I'm going home."

He presses the rolled map into your hands. "I only carried it because I carry everything."

In one corner, in faded ink and a different hand, a passage is marked that you have never seen.

He clanks away down your cleared corridor, humming, frying pan first.
Give him a weapon

You cut him down and put a weapon in his hands. He holds it like a broom.

"I'll just wave it if anything's scary. Things don't like being waved at. I bet."
Heal him

You cut him down. The web has left a red rash up both arms, and he has gone a little purple.

He drinks your potion, blinks twice, and bounces on his toes. "Oh, that's much better. That's like breakfast."
Point the way and walk on

You cut him down and point back the way you came. "That way's safe. I already cleared it."

He shakes your hand with both of his. "You're very kind. Everyone in this place is so kind."
Voices Around the Corner

Three voices, low and angry, just past the next turn.

"You had the map." "No, HE had the map. He carries everything." "So go back and get it." "Past the spider? You go back."

"We didn't lose him. We left him. That's different."

"Not to the map, it isn't."
Sneak past

You keep to the far wall and step only on the silk, where it swallows the sound.

They are still arguing when you reach the next room. They never look up.
Confront them

Three hands go to three weapons, then relax when they see you are alone.

"Your porter is fine," you say. "He thinks he got lost."

They look at their boots. "...Good," the leader mutters at last. "Good for him."
Give them back the map

The leader snatches the map and tucks it away as if it had never left.

Then he pats you on the shoulder. Twice. The way you pat a dog that brought back a stick.

"Decent of you. Very decent. Off you go, then."
